name: Reagan Doctrine
summary: The Reagan Doctrine is the 1980s US policy of openly supporting anti-communist insurgents against Soviet-backed governments (Afghanistan, Nicaragua, Angola, Cambodia), described by supporters as 'containment plus' and by the term's coiner as ex post facto containment at the periphery of the Soviet empire. It rests on moral claims about freedom, strategic claims that Soviet gains must be reversed, and a view that sovereignty cannot shield tyrannies. It is a foreign-policy doctrine and says little on domestic questions.
scope: The foreign-policy doctrine of the Reagan administration as defined by Krauthammer's 1985 Time essay that named it, the encyclopedia entries on it, and the texts those name: the February 1985 State of the Union and Shultz's 22 February 1985 Commonwealth Club address. Reagan's wider domestic programme and other Reagan-era policies are excluded.
